items.question: How long had the master of the Galveston ferry Ray Stoker, Jr. worked at sea overall, and how long had he been on these ferries, when it hit the Coast Guard dock?
items.expected_answer: The captain had over 25 years in the maritime industry but only about 5 months with the ferries.

evidence.quote: a crew of six, consisting of a captain (who had over 25 years in the maritime industry and about 5 months with the ferries), three deckhands, a chief engineer, and an oiler, reported to the vessel.

items.notes: Tests retrieval of the captain's experience, stated parenthetically in the event sequence.

items.question: The ferry Ray Stoker, Jr. experienced a loss of cycloidal propulsion system control while underway from where to where?
items.expected_answer: It was underway from Bolivar to Galveston.

evidence.quote: As of the date of this report, installation was still pending on the remaining two ferries with similar control arrangements. Figure 7. Touch panel with plexiglass cover. (Background source: Texas Department of Transportation) Contact of Ferry Ray Stoker, Jr. with Floating Dock MIR-25-34 11 2 Analysis While the vehicle and passenger ferry Ray Stoker, Jr. was underway from Bolivar to Galveston, the crew experienced a loss of cycloidal propulsion system control (thrust and steering control), and the ferry struck a floating pier at Coast Guard Base Galveston before grounding and coming to a stop.
